messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert: Elevated SRV lookup error rate in us-east-2b. Service discovery timeouts observed across multiple clusters. Paging oncall: tilly (oncall). Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/srv-lookup|srv-lookup>

tilly (oncall): saw the page, jumping in. any customer-facing symptoms?

jen (ops-lead): some internal APIs are returning 503s sporadically; external API edge looks OK so far but internal task queues are backing up. working hypothesis: resolver cache or upstream stub resolver in az.

raj (network-eng): I'm seeing increased TCP retransmits between us-east-2b and our metadata/consul proxies. Could be AZ peering hiccup; checking fabric alerts.

carlos (sre): digging into CoreDNS pods logs in east2b: lots of "cache entry invalidation" and repeated SRV lookups. snippet: 
```
2025-05-10T16:12:04Z coredns[main] ERROR lookup: lookup _svc._tcp.cluster.local: no such host
2025-05-10T16:12:04Z coredns[main] WARN cache: negative entry expired prematurely
```
Also consul clients are reporting intermittent "no healthy upstream" on SRV queries.

maya (platform): there was a small peering config push ~15min before page to VPC edge in east2b (change id: vpc-peering-1743). Rollback is possible but will cause a short control-plane blip.

tilly (oncall): can we confirm if this is limited to east2b? run `dig SRV _svc._tcp.cluster.local @10.10.2.5` from a node in east2b and east2a.

carlos (sre): results: 
- from east2b: `;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, questions: 1`
- from east2a: normal SRV responses.

raj (network-eng): fabric logs show intermittent packet drops on the east2b edge during the window. I'm escalating to cloud network team now.

tilly (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) route around east2b for service discovery traffic by updating resolver policy to prefer east2a, 2) restart CoreDNS pods in east2b to clear cache, 3) if not recovered, rollback peering change. I'll start #1 and #2 now.

maya (platform): +1 on staged approach. I'm preparing the rollback but won't trigger unless the restart + routing doesn't recover within 10m.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by tilly: resolver-policy update to prefer us-east-2a for SRV queries (change: resolver-favor-east2a-2051112345). CI: green, applying to global-config namespace.

carlos (sre): restarting coredns in cluster us-east-2b: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns --grace-period=30`

jen (ops-lead): notify customers: internal ops slack + status page note drafted: "We are investigating internal service discovery errors affecting some background jobs in us-east-2b; no external customer-facing errors observed at this time." ping me for final copy.

raj (network-eng): after policy change, I'm seeing SRV queries from the control-plane go to east2a resolvers instead of east2b. latency to resolver increased slightly but successful responses now.

carlos (sre): CoreDNS pods restarted; logs show normal SRV responses starting at 16:22:11Z. example: `;; ANSWER SECTION: _svc._tcp.cluster.local. 30 IN SRV 10 50 8080 svc-abc.namespace.svc.cluster.local.`

tilly (oncall): monitoring for 15m. if error rate stays low we can de-escalate. Will keep status page updated.

incident-bot: Metric alert cleared: SRV lookup error rate back to normal in us-east-2b (25m after page).

maya (platform): we held off on rollback. network team confirms peering config was fine; root cause likely transient hardware queue in east2b edge switch + CoreDNS cache reacting poorly to the transient negative responses.

jen (ops-lead): customer impact assessment: internal jobs in us-east-2b saw ~12% failure rate for 25m, causing delayed processing for some customers' background workflows. No permanent data loss. Impacted customer list attached in ops doc (link: <https://redwood.internal/incidents/2051112345/postmortem>).

tilly (oncall): current status: mitigated -> monitoring. postmortem owner: jen. follow-ups: 1) add defensive negative-cache backoff to CoreDNS config, 2) add automated resolver failover to prefer other AZs on SRV SERVFAIL spikes, 3) runbook update for peering-change rollback thresholds.

jen (ops-lead): assigning action items in tickets. thanks all for quick response. :thumbsup:

carlos (sre): will attach logs and pod traces to the postmortem.

raj (network-eng): monitoring fabric, will post any followup if cloud provider finds hardware issue.

tilly (oncall): handoff to night oncall at 19:00 UTC; leaving this open until postmortem posted.

incident-bot: Incident state changed: RESOLVED -> MONITORING. Incident ID: IR-2051112345."
